assessment: In their paper, Hernandez-Perez et al. perform a detailed and solid analysis of kazrin, a widely expressed protein that appears to be involved in many diverse cellular processes, but whose exact function is unknown. The authors employ mouse embryonic fibroblasts and biochemistry to investigate the function of Kazrin and determine that Kazrin promotes the dynein/dynactin-dependent transport of early endosomes. These valuable findings will be of interest to those in the field of intracellular transport.
